lines.speaker: Diogenes
lines.text: Hey, Carian, what makes you think you're so great that you deserve to be ranked above all the rest of us?

lines.speaker: Mausolus
lines.text: For my kingship, Sinopian. I ruled all of Caria, governed some of the Lydians too, subjected a few islands, and pushed as far as Miletus conquering most of Ionia. I was handsome and tall and tough in battle. But the biggest thing: in Halicarnassus I have an enormous tomb lying over me, bigger than any other dead man's, and none so beautifully decorated, with horses and men sculpted in the finest stone with perfect accuracy—you wouldn't easily find a temple like it. Don't you think I have a right to be proud of these things?

lines.speaker: Diogenes
lines.text: For the kingship and the beauty and the weight of the tomb?

lines.speaker: Diogenes
lines.text: But, my dear Mausolus, that strength and that looks aren't with you anymore. If we picked a beauty judge, I couldn't tell you why your skull should be preferred to mine. We're both bald and bare, we grin the same way with our teeth, we've lost our eyes, and our noses are flattened. As for the tomb and those pricey stones, maybe the Halicarnassians can show them off to foreigners and boast about their great building. But you, my good man, I don't see what you get out of it—unless you're saying you're carrying a heavier load than the rest of us, crushed under all that stone.

lines.speaker: Mausolus
lines.text: So all that was pointless for me, and Mausolus is going to be equal in honor to Diogenes?

lines.speaker: Diogenes
lines.text: Not equal, my noble friend, not at all. Mausolus will moan, remembering the life above ground where he thought he was happy, while Diogenes will be laughing at him. The one will talk about the tomb in Halicarnassus built by his wife and sister Artemisia, but Diogenes doesn't even know if his body has a tomb—he never cared about it. Instead he's left the best men a story about himself, having lived a higher life than your monument, you most slavish of Carians, and in a more lasting place.
